definitions.explanation: A person who is excessively kind and trusting, often to the point of being naive or easily taken advantage of. Can be used affectionately or critically.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧お{人好|ひとよ}しだ⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{断|ことわ}れない→断る：02102_kotowaru⟧。
⟦そんな→そんな：01645_sonna⟧お{人好|ひとよ}しだ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{騙|だま}される→騙す：02286_damasu⟧⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
examples.english: If you're that gullible, you'll get tricked.

examples.japanese: ⟦{母|はは}→母：00549_haha⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧お{人好|ひとよ}しで、⟦{頼|たの}まれる→頼む：01104_tanomu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{何|なん}→何〜：03100_nan⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{引|ひ}き{受|う}けて→引き受ける：03140_hikiukeru⟧しまう。
examples.english: My mother is such a pushover that she takes on anything she's asked to do.

notes:
The nuance ranges from warm affection to gentle criticism depending on context. When used about someone you care about, it often carries a tone of "too kind for their own good." When used more critically, it implies the person is naive or a pushover. Composed of the honorific お + ⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ (person) + {好|よ}し (good-natured).

USAGE:
Can function as a noun (「お{人好|ひとよ}しだ」) or as a modifier with ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ (「お{人好|ひとよ}し⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{性格|せいかく}→性格：03371_seikaku⟧」). Often used with だ⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧ to explain why someone gets taken advantage of.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{人好|ひとよ}しな⟦{性格|せいかく}→性格：03371_seikaku⟧: a too-nice personality
- お{人好|ひとよ}し⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{程|ほど}→程：01724_hodo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧: there's a limit to being too nice
- お{人好|ひとよ}しだ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{損|そん}をする→損をする：30214_sonwosuru⟧: being too nice will cost you

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧: good-natured — a neutral description without the "too much" nuance
- お{人好|ひとよ}し is stronger, implying naivety
- ⟦{甘|あま}い→甘い：00617_amai⟧: lenient; soft — describes someone who is too easy on others
- ⟦{世間知|せけんし}らず→世間知らず：22674_sekenshirazu⟧: naive about the world — more about lacking worldly experience
